title: Jobs from three actions
prompt: What does this program print? Six of the 12 lesson trips are longer than 3 miles, and they use 2 different rate codes. Type each printed line on its own line.
program:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "false")
sc = spark.sparkContext
tracker = sc.statusTracker()

long_trips = trips.filter(F.col("trip_distance") > 3)
by_rate = long_trips.groupBy("rate_code").count()
plan = by_rate._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
print(plan.count("Exchange"))

sc.setJobGroup("actions", "three actions")
first = long_trips.first()
n = long_trips.count()
rows = by_rate.collect()
jobs = sorted(tracker.getJobIdsForGroup("actions"))
print(len(jobs))
print([len(tracker.getJobInfo(j).stageIds) for j in jobs])
print(n, len(rows))
hints: Building `by_rate` and printing its plan start no job. Grouping adds one `Exchange`.
Each of `first()`, `count()` and `collect()` starts its own job.
`count()` on a DataFrame adds up partial counts after a small shuffle, so its job has two stages.
